answer: A sybil operator saves money by letting clones share one memory: whatever one learns, all know. So test for unearned transfer. Give each identity a different private drill: one judges zephyr gusts, one mixes a pigment ratio, one charts a delta current. Later test every identity on all three. Honest agents improve only on their own; clones jump on drills they never practised, the lesson having leaked across names. Merge identities whose gains track each other's drills and pay once. Sandboxing each clone stops the leak but kills the shared-learning saving that made the farm profitable.
